title: במדבר פרק 25
english: And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.
And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baalpeor.

And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.
And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.
Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace:
And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.
Now the name of the Israelite that was slain, even that was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.
And the name of the Midianitish woman that was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he was head over a people, and of a chief house in Midian.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Vex the Midianites, and smite them:

For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor's sake.
ai_explanation: עם ישראל ישב בשטים, מקום ליד מואב עם עצי שיטה. שם החל העם לזנות עם בנות מואב.
בעקבות הזנות, הנשים המואביות קראו לעם ישראל להשתתף בזבחי אלוהיהן. העם אכל מהזבחים והשתחווה לאלוהיהן, מכיוון שהצטרפו לפולחנים מתוך עניינם בנשות המקום, ולא הגיעו לכך מראש במטרה לעבוד עבודה זרה.
בסופו של דבר, ישראל נצמדו לבעל פעור, שהיה האל המואבי השליט באזור. כתוצאה מכך, ה' כעס על ישראל בגלל הזנות והעבודה הזרה.

ה' ציווה את משה לקחת את כל ראשי העם, שהם השופטים המופקדים על הריגת החוטאים. מכיוון שאיש לא מחה בידיהם עד כה, ה' הורה להרוג ולתלות בפומבי את המשתתפים בחטא, כדי להביע את חומרת המעשה ולשיב את כעסו מישראל.
משה אמר לשופטי ישראל, המנהיגים הממונים על העם, שכל אחד יהרוג את האנשים שבפיקוחו אשר נצמדו לבעל פעור.
אדם חשוב מבני ישראל הגיע והביא עמו מדינית אל אוהל, לעיני משה וכל עדת בני ישראל. הוא עשה זאת בפומבי כדי להצהיר שאין בכך פסול, בזמן שהעם בכה בפתח אוהל מועד משום שחשו שהמעשה מגונה אך היו חסרי אונים.
פינחס בן אלעזר בן אהרן הכהן, נכדו של הכהן הגדול, ראה את המעשה החמור. הוא קם מתוך העדה ולקח רומח בידו, כיוון שנכח באותו מעמד עם משה ושאר המנהיגים.
פינחס הלך אחרי איש ישראל והמדינית אל האוהל, ודקר את שניהם בשעת מעשה ממש. הוא דקר את איש ישראל ואת האישה באבר מינה. בעקבות דקירה זו, המגפה נעצרה מעל בני ישראל.
מספר המתים במגפה עמד על עשרים וארבעה אלף איש.
ה' דיבר אל משה ואמר לו.

פינחס בן אלעזר בן אהרן הכהן שיכך והרגיע את כעס ה' מעל בני ישראל, בכך שקנא לקנאתו בתוכם. פינחס חש צורך לשמור בקנאות על נוכחותו המוחלטת של ה' בקרב העם ולכן עשה מעשה קיצוני שלא צווה, ולולא מעשה זה, המגפה הייתה מתפשטת על כל העם.

ה' אמר שייתן לפינחס את "בריתי שלום" המיוחדת. ברית השלום ניתנה לו לא כי הוא איש שלום, אלא כי השכין שלום בין ישראל לאביהם שבשמיים, ובכך הכריז על בעלותו הבלעדית של ה' על ישראל ועל אי השלמה עם התערבות גורם זר בקשר ביניהם.
פינחס קיבל מתנה של ברית כהונת עולם לו ולזרעו אחריו. הוא קיבל זאת כי קנא לאלוהיו וכיפר על בני ישראל.
שמו של איש ישראל שהוכה יחד עם המדיינית הוא זמרי בן סלוא. הוא היה נשיא בית אב לשבט השמעוני.
האשה המדיינית שהוכתה נקראה כזבי בת צור. צור היה ראש אומות בית אב במדין, כלומר מנהיג בית האב הגדול או החשוב ביותר. המדינים היו שבטים שונים שהיו להם קשרים.
ה' ציווה לשנוא את המדיינים ולהכות אותם. בעוד שעל מואב ה' הגן, במדיין הוא ציווה להילחם.
המדיינים הם אויבים לישראל בגלל תחבולותיהם שזממו נגדם בענייני פעור ובעניין כזבי בת נשיא מדין. מזימת הפיתוי באמצעות הבנות הייתה מתוכננת על ידי בלעם והמדיינים כדי להחטיא את ישראל ולגרום להם למפלה.
ai_explanation_en: Steinsaltz identifies Shittim as a place near Moab, likely named for the acacia trees that grew there. In this location, the Israelites began to engage in whoredom with the Moabite women.

Following the sexual relations, the Moabite women invited the Israelites to sacrifices for their gods, where the people ate and bowed down. Steinsaltz clarifies that the Israelites did not initially intend idolatry, but joined these foreign cults due to their involvement with the women.
Ultimately, Israel became attached to Baal-Peor, identified as the Moabite god ruling that region. Consequently, the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel due to both the whoredom and the idolatry.

God instructed Moses to gather all the heads of the people, understood as the judges responsible for executing transgressors. Since no one had yet acted, God commanded these judges to kill and publicly hang those who participated in the sin, against the sun, to demonstrate the severity of the act and avert God's fierce anger from Israel.
Moses commanded the judges of Israel, who were the appointed leaders, that each should kill the men under their charge who had joined themselves to Baal-Peor.

An important man among the Israelites publicly brought a Midianitish woman he found in the market into his tent, in the sight of Moses and the entire weeping congregation. He performed this brazen act to declare it acceptable, while the other Israelites at the Tent of Meeting were distraught but helpless, unsure how to respond to the grave offense.
Phinehas, grandson of the High Priest Aaron and son of Eleazar, witnessed this act while present with Moses and other leaders. He rose from the congregation and took a javelin in his hand.

Phinehas followed the Israelite man and the Midianitish woman into their tent and stabbed both of them directly during their act, specifically piercing the woman through her sexual organ. As a result of this action, the plague among the children of Israel was halted.
The total number of people who died in the plague was twenty-four thousand.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, calmed and appeased God's anger from the Israelites by zealously expressing God's jealousy among them. Phinehas felt compelled to guard God's absolute presence among Israel, performing an extreme act not explicitly commanded. God states that His jealousy would have otherwise consumed all the children of Israel through the spreading plague.

Therefore, God declared He would grant Phinehas His covenant of peace. This covenant was given not because Phinehas was inherently peaceful, but because he established peace between Israel and God. Through his zealous act, Phinehas affirmed God's exclusive claim over Israel, a stance that does not tolerate any foreign interference in the intimate relationship between God and His people.

Steinsaltz clarifies that the "everlasting covenant of priesthood" is the specific gift Pinchas received. This reward was bestowed because of his zealous act for God and his subsequent atonement for the Israelites.

Steinsaltz emphasizes that Zimri was "slain with the Midianitish woman at the time of the deed," specifying the context of his death. He reiterates Zimri's identity as a prince of a Simeonite chief house.

Steinsaltz identifies Cozbi as the daughter of Zur, who was a leader of various Midianite tribes. He clarifies that Midian consisted of different tribes connected to one another, and Zur specifically led their largest or most significant chief house.
Steinsaltz's commentary simply restates the biblical phrase, indicating a direct transition to the divine command that follows.
Steinsaltz interprets "Vex" (צָרוֹר) as "hate," instructing Israel to both hate and strike the Midianites. He notes that God protected Moab but mandated warfare specifically against Midian.

Steinsaltz clarifies that the Midianites vexed Israel with "schemes" and "plotted" against them regarding Peor and Cozbi. He explains that the plan to seduce Israel with their daughters, including a princely daughter, was a deliberate plot by Balaam and the Midianites. This was an attempt to undermine Israel's existence by attacking their holiness and uniqueness, revealing the Midianites' greater hatred compared to the Moabites.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know that "Baal Peor" is a combination of the name "Baal," a common Canaanite deity, and "Peor," which may refer to the place of worship or a specific form of licentious worship?
